settings.copy: Ember & Air is a working glass studio where the furnace never goes cold. Watch a gather of molten glass become a bowl, a vase, or a paperweight — then try it yourself at the bench with a gaffer who's been at the pipe for twenty years.

settings.title: How a piece
settings.intro: Every piece on our shelves took the same patient journey through heat and air. Here's the path from a gather of molten glass to a piece you can hold, pour from, and keep.

steps.title: Gather & blow
steps.text: You dip the pipe into the furnace and gather a ball of molten glass, then blow the first bubble. Beginners get a steady hand on theirs until the first shape stands.

steps.title: Shape & marver
steps.text: Once the glass is on the bench, you roll it on the marver, shape it with blocks and jacks, and pull the walls where you want them. This is where a piece starts to feel like yours.

steps.title: Add color & detail
steps.text: You pick up frit, cane, or a second gather of color, then twist, trail, or blow it into the surface. The palette is yours to choose from our color wall.

steps.title: Anneal & cool
steps.text: The finished piece goes into the annealer to cool slowly over a day — so it comes out strong, clear, and ready to take home.

settings.note: Ember & Air is built on patience: if a piece cracks or slumps in the annealer, we don't call it a failure — we call it a lesson, and we gather again until you're proud of what you made.

settings.title: A studio that
settings.intro: Whether you've never touched a blowpipe or you're returning after years away, the studio is set up to let you work at your own pace — with real guidance, never hovering.

features.title: Small, unhurried benches
features.text: Four benches, four students, one gaffer. You get the attention you need without feeling watched — and the shop stays calm enough to actually focus.

features.title: Everything included
features.text: Glass, color, tools, and annealing are part of every session. You never pay extra to see your work finished — it's all in the price.

features.title: A furnace that never sleeps
features.text: Our furnace runs every day, so the shop is always warm and your pieces come home on a schedule you can count on.

features.title: For every level
features.text: From a first-ever paperweight to advanced color work, the studio has a place for you. Returning students get open-bench time and their own shelf.

features.title: A gaffer who stays
features.text: Our lead gaffer has blown in this same room for twenty years. They know exactly when to step in and when to let a wobble become a lesson.

features.title: Work you can keep
features.text: Every piece you make is yours — annealed, cooled, and ready to hold. Your shelf at home grows with every class.

settings.title: The feeling of
settings.intro: People come for a class and stay for a season. Here's a little of what they tell us as they carry their work home.

reviews.quote: I came in convinced I had no hand for it. Three months later I've got a shelf of bowls I actually use every morning. The gaffer never once made me feel like I was behind.
reviews.author: Priya Raman

reviews.quote: The small benches are the whole difference. Four of us, one patient gaffer, and a furnace that runs every day. My pieces actually come home — that's rarer than you'd think.
reviews.author: Marcus Bell

reviews.quote: I'd blown in college and wanted to come back to it. This studio gave me open time, my own shelf, and zero pressure. It's the calmest two hours of my week.
reviews.author: Elena Ortiz
